t.E570.agn: In 2017, EFSA referred to the group ADI 'not specified' set by the SCF in 1991 and found no safety concern at the reported uses and use levels.
t.E570.body: These fatty acids occur naturally in dietary fats and are used for energy in the body like other fatty acids.
t.E570.eval: The fatty acid source may be vegetable or animal (including beef/pork); the source is often not stated on the label.
t.E570.prod: Fatty acids (e.g. stearic acid) are obtained by hydrolysis of animal or vegetable fats.
t.E570.regx.0: Re-evaluated; no numerical ADI needed ('not specified'); no safety concern at the reported uses.
t.E570.summary: Fatty acids obtained from vegetable or animal fats (stearic acid, etc.). Used as an emulsifier, coating and tableting aid.
t.E570.what: Fatty acids (stearic, palmitic, myristic, oleic acid) used as glazing agents, anti-caking agents and emulsifiers.
